# External release gate: pending semantic inventories

`cargo xtask check-conformance` and `check-external-release` use the canonical
stage2 requirement format. Ordinary mode checks integrity and exits0 for a valid
pending report. `--strict` still exits1 while any required review, case, profile,
direction or source-bound evidence remains unresolved. Ordinary success and
checker implementation are not protocol implementation or release passes.

Stage2 preserves the entire stage1 external floor:34 subsystem owners, eight
foundations,677 registry identities including aliases and zero-use identities,
99 partial node messages,34 operations, three profiles and156 original cases.
All734 original review obligations remain unknown with their exact identities,
reasons and scope. No draft or receipt can waive them. C helper/function names,
signatures, queues, scheduler, plugin ABI or process organization remain outside
the implicit Rust requirement matrix.

## Production operation entry mapping

[operation-entrypoints.json](operation-entrypoints.json) maps305 external operation
groups across all42 required owners to actual Rust production entries and fixed
official sources. Source entries are present for all305 mapped groups, with no
remaining confirmed gaps in this finite entry map. TRANSPORT monitoring and link
enumeration include the actual service, native client, SDK and ordinary CLI.
`present` locates an implementation entry; it does not certify every message,
profile, edge condition or runtime behavior. Complete entry navigation is separate
from complete semantic inventory and official interoperability acceptance.

This navigation ledger preserves all required owners and qualifies its named
source hashes. It neither resolves the canonical unknowns below nor supplies
semantic review, interoperability receipts or release credit. Source fixes for
three snapshot recovery callers retain their pending runtime acceptance.

## Additive FS draft

`semantic/fs.json` expresses38 FS capability contracts,147 planned cases and18
candidate profiles, with all23 FS registry identities. Each operation cites exact
original source hashes and line anchors from the pinned2193-path survey. Cases
and profiles reference each other explicitly. Every review state is draft,
profile/direction review is pending, and evidence slots are empty. The inventory
has no authoritative implementation-status or old-audit import fields.

The draft includes public artifacts, full content trees, metadata/directories,
UBLOCKs, normalization, publication/search/download, indexing, actual service
IPC, anonymous CORE routing, directed CADET transfers, migration, persistence,
resources and substantive user operations. The optional official publish-helper
IPC profile does not mandate C helper processes; metadata scanning/extraction
remains required. Same-ID FS_PUT client and peer layouts stay separate operations.
The fixed content encoding is AEAD; the draft is not limited to an8MiB first tree
implementation or the already admitted URI layer.

The report now has303 pending cases:156 retained cases plus147 draft FS cases.
These are draft review/evidence obligations, not303 observed failures, missing
functions or a permanent C-helper floor. The report separately identifies the
conditional helper operation and its four draft cases. A later independently
reviewed architecture/boundary choice may classify the helper profile as
nonselected while preserving required Rust-native scanning/extraction. Draft
status strings, unsupported nonselection claims and passing evidence cannot
erase any original unknown. Pending inventory operations/profiles/registry classifications are
reported separately. No case, source-file count or successful parser marks a
semantic owner complete. Required build/platform, living-standard, non-C,
submodule and cross-owner surveys remain pending too.

`semantic-inventory.schema.json` publishes the closed draft shape; `semantic.py`
validates the actual references, unique identities, source-index membership and
hashes, case ownership, profile candidate directions and registry floor. With
`GNUNET_REFERENCE_SOURCE`, actual original file bytes, line anchors and ranges
are checked in addition to the unchanged complete tracked-source survey before
and after verification. No C build, service or network operation runs here.

`release-lock.json` binds the additive requirement/schema/inventory references
and exact stage1 predecessor. Its independently pinned checksum prevents
silently deleting the FS extension, editing its cases/source anchors or
regenerating a reduced lock. Draft-to-reviewed claims are rejected; this stage
introduces no review-resolution authority or evidence adapter. A later review
model must explicitly establish complete reviewed contracts and permitted
case/profile/direction slots before results can satisfy them.

## Historical stage1 and readiness

The five original stage1 data files are retained byte-for-byte under
`history/stage1/`. They remain explicitly readable with:

```sh
python3 -B tools/external-contracts/release.py --historical-stage1
python3 -B tools/external-contracts/release.py --historical-stage1 --strict
```

The first reports the old734 unknowns/156 pending cases. The second refuses a
release. Canonical mode never silently accepts a stage1 lock as a downgrade.
Historical reading is an audit capability, not old private-protocol migration.

Readiness is derived from validated unresolved review obligations, pending
cases/slots, pending semantic review and actual reference-source checking. A
result status or Boolean cannot resolve those inputs. The current preserved
unknowns and drafts make `complete_semantic_inventory`, `release_ready` and
`full_GNUnet_conformance_verified` false. The basic aggregate is no longer a
permanent hardcoded false response; review/producer migrations and real required
behavior must still be completed before a future release can satisfy it.

## Evidence remains separate

`release-evidence.schema.json` retains the closed source-bound receipt format.
The checker verifies original actor binaries, compiler/build provenance,
configured/generated/dependency inputs, current implementation/reference maps,
loaded file hashes, exits, raw artifacts and exact semantic-adapter verdicts.
Legacy C-helper catalogs remain excluded from the implementation map; mandatory
owner flags and the external floor remain independently checked. Shared-cache
UUID-only observations are not file-content hashes.

The adapter registry and evidence index remain empty. FS draft case/profile IDs
cannot be used as reviewed receipt targets, even by supplying a fake passing
adapter. Existing URI/component/network audits are not wrapped or relabeled into
formal release receipts. No production C FFI, response generator or substitute
service earns credit. A future reviewed adapter reads frozen artifacts only and
must verify the exact unchanged receipt; it may not execute new network profiles.

Run `python3 -B tools/external-contracts/release_tests.py` for local integrity and
rejection controls. They include synthetic integrity fixtures, not actual GNUnet
protocol evidence. Tests preserve owner/alias/case floors, historical readability,
unknown refusal and actor provenance, and reject semantic omissions, source/hash/
anchor tamper, mismatched profiles/directions, self-awarded review, fake draft
receipts and canonical downgrade. Rust architecture/resource correctness,
complete Node/platform interoperability and measured performance stay separate
required work.
